data.title: Disulfide mapping of J-chain by crosslinking MS
data.projectDescription: Here we show how J-chain (JC) outcompetes the sixth IgM subunit during assembly. We looked at the disulfide re-arrangements in JC and showed that it exists as an unstructured protein with non-native disulfides before its insertion into IgM.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: 15 µL of protein (about 1 mg/mL) were mixed with 15 µL of 8 M Urea in 50 mM Tris and incubated for 30 min at room temperature. All samples were denatured at 56 C for 30 min. Then 4.5 µL of 100 mM 2-Iodoacetamide were added and the samples were incubated for 20 min at room temperature in the dark. Samples were then precipitated with 40 volumes of ice-cold ethanol and incubated at -20 C for 1 h. The samples were centrifuged at 16 000 rpm for 8 min and supernatant (s/n) was discarded. The pellets were then washed with 200 µL of ethanol, the s/n was discarded, the samples were air-dried for 10 min. Then 100 µL of 50% ACN were added and the samples were dried in a SpeedVac concentrator for 2 h. The pellets were diluted in 49 µL of 2 M Urea, 10 mM CaCl2, 0.2 M Tris pH 6.7. Then, 1 µL of Trypsin (0.5 µg/µL) was added and the reaction was held overnight at 37 C. The samples were then cleaved with 5 µL of 0.2 µg/µL Asp-N protease and incubated for 8 h at 37C. To stop the reaction, 1 µL of 100% FA was added and the samples were stored overnight at -80 C. The samples were then desalted with the double C18 layer stage tips. The samples were applied onto the tips and washed 3 times with 70 µL of 0.5% FA by mild centrifugation. The peptides were eluted with two times 30 µL of 80 % ACN, 0.5% FA via centrifugation and dried in a SpeedVac concentrator for 2 h. For the MS/MS measurements, the peptides were dissolved in 25 µL of 0.5 % FA and sonicated in an ultrasonic bath at room temperature for 15 min. The peptides were filtered with 0.22 µM centrifugal filters for 1 min at 7000 g.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: The samples were measured on Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid instrument (Thermo Fisher). The raw data were converted to mxXML files using MSConvert, analysed with Kojak and peclorator and visualised with ProXL.
